historical_claims.anchor: Toni Morrison was born Chloe Ardelia Wofford in Lorain, Ohio, in 1931.
historical_claims.source_locator: NEA Big Read: Toni Morrison biography

historical_claims.anchor: At Random House she helped bring Black writers and thinkers into a publishing system that had too often treated their experiences as marginal.
historical_claims.source_locator: NEA: senior editor and publishing of authors

historical_claims.anchor: One project was The Black Book, a 1974 collection of archival materials about Black American experience, edited and assembled through a collaboration involving Middleton A. Harris and others, with Morrison as an important editorial participant
historical_claims.source_locator: NEA: The Black Book; Lehigh Garner clipping history

historical_claims.anchor: Among the documents she encountered was a newspaper account of Margaret Garner, an enslaved woman who escaped with her family to Ohio in 1856 and killed a child when capture threatened.
historical_claims.source_locator: NEA and Lehigh: historical Garner case

historical_claims.anchor: One striking difference is that Sethe and Denver remain alive and free at the novel's close, while Margaret Garner was recaptured and died enslaved.
historical_claims.source_locator: Lehigh: specific differences between Garner and Sethe

historical_claims.anchor: In an interview published by the National Endowment for the Arts, Morrison explained a discovery she made while writing: the dead daughter had to be allowed to respond.
historical_claims.source_locator: NEA 2015 interview: dead daughter as necessary perspective

historical_claims.anchor: The novel begins after almost all of this has happened.

work.note: Existing survey chapter label '1987 · Beloved' supplies the work's publication year; bibliography identifies the work. This dates publication, not its fictional setting or the lecture's creation.

description: Studies Toni Morrison’s Beloved through Sethe’s fractured memories, the haunting of a household, motherhood under slavery, and the novel’s shifting order of revelation.
